title: Graceful API degradation for unavailable backends with probabilistic KV skipping
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Our API frontends are currently vulnerable to sudden downstream slowdowns (Redis/KV and read-only DB) where connection pools fill and tail latency spikes. Full circuit opens are blunt and can cause visible errors to customers. We need a softer degradation mode that preserves availability and reasonable latency while shedding load in a controlled manner.

Goal:
Introduce a per-route, per-tenant adaptive degradation policy combining: 1) probabilistic KV-skip (skip non-critical KV/cache reads with tunable probability), 2) connection pool admission throttles that reject or queue low-priority requests, and 3) a hybrid circuit-breaker that moves into a degraded state before opening. The aim is to keep 95th percentile API latency within SLOs (target: 95th < 200ms for read-heavy endpoints) and reduce error budget burn during downstream incidents.

Scope:
- Server-side runtime changes to support probabilistic KV skipping and priority-marked requests.
- Connection pool admission controls and soft-rejection path for low-priority requests.
- Hybrid circuit-breaker state machine (healthy -> degraded -> open) using slow-percentile and error-rate signals.
- Console/metrics: new dashboards and alerts, rollout behind feature flag and per-tenant config.

Non-goals:
- Full rewrite of pooling implementation. We will augment existing pool with admission layers.
- Changes to client SDKs beyond labeling requests for priority (handled server-side where possible).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Probabilistic KV-skip can be enabled per-route; measured skipped-read rate matches configured probability within +/-5% over 1 hour
A2: During simulated Redis latency injection (95th=1s), endpoints with KV-skip+degraded pool maintain 95th API latency < 200ms for >= 80% of tenants annotated as high-priority
A3: Hybrid circuit-breaker emits transition events to tracing and console; degraded state reduces downstream concurrency by >= 40% on average
A4: New dashboards show per-tenant skipped-read rate, pool-rejections, degraded-state-duration, and customer-impact estimates
A5: Canary rollout to 10% of traffic with feature flag and automatic rollback on regression (error-rate increase > 2x baseline or 95th latency > 300ms for 10m)
A6: Unit and integration tests for key code paths; load-test artifacts and JMeter script linked in ticket
design_decisions: D1: Use probabilistic skipping (Bernoulli sampling) rather than TTL-based eviction to avoid global cache churn spikes
D2: Treat KV-skip as eventually-consistent optimization: skipped reads return fallback empty/placeholder or trigger background population depending on route policy
D3: Implement admission control at connpool entry — two lanes (priority and best-effort). Best-effort gets soft rejections with HTTP 503-shed or degraded payloads based on route config

D4: Hybrid circuit-breaker uses a move to 'degraded' when slow-percentile (p95) of downstream exceeds threshold for window T, and only moves to 'open' on sustained high error-rate to prioritize availability
D5: Expose runtime flags + per-tenant knobs in remote config service; safe defaults applied for existing tenants
tasks: T1: Prototype probabilistic KV-skip utility and inject into example route (ENG sandbox)
T2: Add connpool admission layer with configurable priority lanes and metrics
T3: Implement hybrid circuit-breaker state machine and events for tracing
T4: Add feature flag and per-tenant UI in Console to toggle/adjust probability and thresholds
T5: Create load test plan and run chaos test injecting Redis/KV latency/FAILS
T6: Instrument dashboards and alerts; add playbook for on-call
T7: PR reviews, security review, and canary deployment
notes: 2025-11-16 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting with runtime and infra. Agreed on Bernoulli sampling to minimize coupling with cache internals.
2025-11-20 - Marco Chen: Prototype shows 35% reduction in pool occupancy when skip probability is 0.4 on read-heavy traces (sandbox run). CPU overhead negligible.
2025-11-25 - Design review: PM and SRE suggested conservative default p=0.1 and per-tenant max of 0.6. Also requested ability to return 'degraded but served' payloads for certain endpoints.
2025-12-01 - Load test planned: chaos script prepared at https://github.com/redwood-inference/chaos-tests/tree/main/kv-latency (JMeter + client harness).
2025-12-02 - Security: initial review indicated no new secrets; KMS/HSM not impacted. Security to do a short checklist before canary.
comments: 2025-11-30 - Marco Chen: Found edge case where skipping a KV read for endpoints that populate short-lived tokens caused downstream auth errors. Mitigation: add allowlist of routes that cannot skip. (action: add route allowlist)
2025-12-01 - SRE - Priya Rao: Recommend adding a rolling window metric for slow-percentile triggers to avoid flapping during transient noise. We'll add hysteresis to state transitions.
2025-12-02 - Aisha Patel: Plan to canary at 10% traffic next Wednesday. If canary stable for 24h, gradual ramp to 50% with telemetry checks. Contingency: immediate rollback via feature flag toggle.
